universe.title: 🌐 Parcel Universe
universe.question: 🌐 Parcel Universe
universe.lede: Every parcel, sold or not, as it is now: what's valued. Please provide the file that contains your parcel GEOMETRY as well as your primary parcel ID.

sales.title: 💰 Sales Record
sales.question: Which file is your 💰 Sales Record?
sales.lede: One row per sale: what the models learn from. Pick it here; its date, its IDs and the rest come one by one in the next steps. Files with more about each sale (deeds, say) come later: just pick the main one for now.

sales_ids.title: IDs
sales_ids.question: How does each sale find its parcel?
sales_ids.lede: The parcel ID each sale carries, and the sale''s own ID: a column, or made from the parcel ID and the sale date. Each sale must find its parcel in the parcel universe.

sale_price.title: Sale price
sale_price.question: What did each sell for?
sale_price.lede: The price paid. Amounts are read exactly as OpenAVMKit will read them: currency signs, spaces and the thousands separator are dropped, (10) is −10, and N/A, TBD, - and blanks are missing.

sale_date.title: Sale date
sale_date.question: When was each sold?
sale_date.lede: The date of sale, read exactly as OpenAVMKit will read it. It comes first: a sale ID can be made from the parcel ID and this date.

valid_sale.title: Valid sale
valid_sale.question: Which sales are valid?
valid_sale.lede: Arm''s-length sales, usable for modelling. Say which values mean valid; the price condition leaves out nominal sales.

vacant_sale.title: Vacant sale
vacant_sale.question: Which sales were of vacant land?
vacant_sale.lede: Land with no building when it sold: vacant sales value the land. Say which values mean vacant.

more_add.title: Add files
more_add.question: Any more files to join?
more_add.lede: Just add all the extra files you''ll be using: building details, sale details, more sales… You''ll configure them one by one in the next steps. Permits have a step of their own, later. None? Just go on.

building_size.title: Building size
building_size.question: How big is each building?
building_size.lede: The finished area of the building, in the unit its column is in. Required: every model starts from it.

land_size.title: Land size
land_size.question: How big is each parcel''s land?
land_size.lede: The parcel''s land area. Left out, it''s worked out from each parcel''s shape.

age.title: Age
age.question: How old is each building?
age.lede: When it was built and, if it has one, the year a major renovation makes it act its age from. Strongly recommended.

quality.title: Quality
quality.question: How well is each building built?
quality.lede: One column the models can use. Numbers say which way is better; categories are ranked into tiers, best first, and each tier gets a number.

condition.title: Condition
condition.question: What condition is each building in?
condition.lede: One column the models can use. Numbers say what they mean (% good, years of life left…); categories are ranked into tiers, best first, and each tier gets a number.

address.title: Address
address.question: What is each parcel''s address?
address.lede: The site address of each parcel (its situs), for reports and for finding a parcel. Optional.

coordinates.title: Coordinates
coordinates.question: Where is each parcel?
coordinates.lede: OpenAVMKit works out where each parcel is from its shape: nothing to load. Check the centre the distances and directions are measured from.

location.title: Location fields
location.question: What areas does each parcel belong to?
location.lede: Areas each parcel belongs to: neighborhood, market area, school district, zoning district… Pick the column and give it a name; models use them as categories. Add as many as you like, one at a time.

building.title: Building
building.question: What kind of buildings are they?

rooms_features.title: Rooms & features
rooms_features.question: Rooms and features
rooms_features.lede: Bedrooms, bathrooms, style, materials and systems.

property_type.title: Land use & building type
property_type.question: What kind of property is each parcel?
property_type.lede: Land use, building type and stories: model groups are made from these, after Bring in data. Pick whichever you have; a building description, class or units can be added under More.

custom.title: Your own fields
custom.question: Any other columns to use?
custom.lede: Any other column of a parcel file, under a name you choose. Say whether it''s a land/location, improvement or other field, and whether it''s a category or a number: OpenAVMKit treats them that way when it models.

assessed.title: Existing values
assessed.question: Do you have values to compare the models with?
assessed.lede: The roll, a vendor''s AVM, last year''s values: each set is judged beside the models, on the same sales. A market value is enough; land and improvement values are kept for later.

shapefiles.title: Shapefiles
shapefiles.question: Any map layers?
shapefiles.lede: Zoning, school zones, flood zones, parks, schools… Each layer either stamps its areas onto the parcels inside them, or gives each parcel its distance to the nearest feature.

as_sold.title: Sales record fields
as_sold.question: Does your sales record describe each property as it was when it sold?
as_sold.lede: How sales and parcels each get their characteristics: what the models learn from, and what they value.

condo_ask.title: Do you have condos?
condo_ask.question: Do you have condos?
condo_ask.lede: Or anything else on the roll but not on the map: a unit with a parcel ID of its own but no parcel shape, because it sits on a parcel it shares. OAK box can give each unit the shape of the parcel it''s on, so it''s valued like any other parcel.

condo_file.title: Units file
condo_file.question: Which file has the units?
condo_file.lede: The file whose rows are the units: each with a parcel ID of its own, and no shape of its own. It''s joined on More files like any file with more about each parcel.

condo_rows.title: Which rows
condo_rows.question: Which rows are units?
condo_rows.lede: Usually every row of the units file without a shape. If the file mixes units with other things that have no shape (mineral or air rights, business property, a building''s common areas), say which rows are units: the rest are left out.

condo_link.title: The parcel they''re on
condo_link.question: How does each unit find the parcel it''s on?
condo_link.lede: A unit takes the shape of the parcel it sits on: its building, complex or park. Often the unit''s ID starts with that parcel''s; sometimes a column names it.

condo_land.title: Land
condo_land.question: How much land is each unit''s?
condo_land.lede: Land is a big part of a parcel''s value. Say how the shared parcel''s land (its shape''s area) is split among its units, or whether they have none of their own. The examples show what each unit gets.

condo_fields.title: Their fields
condo_fields.question: What should the units carry?
condo_fields.lede: A unit sits on a parcel it shares: where it is and the land it''s on are the parcel''s. What its building is like comes from the units file.

condo_location.title: As a location
condo_location.question: Treat each shared parcel as a location?
condo_location.lede: Units on one parcel share a lot: the building, its amenities, an association. As a location, like a neighborhood, models can learn what being on each one is worth.

condo_summary.title: Summary
condo_summary.question: Here''s what happens to the units
condo_summary.lede: When Bring in data runs, OpenAVMKit does this, in this order. Change any part from the steps on the left.

deeds.title: Deeds
deeds.question: Which deed was each sale recorded under?
deeds.lede: The deed ID, or the deed book and page. Several sales on one deed, on the same day, are usually one sale of several parcels: sales scrutiny (notebook 2) finds them this way and sets them aside. No deeds? Skip it.

permits.title: Permits
permits.question: Do you have building permits?
permits.lede: A sale followed soon by a demolition permit was really a sale of the land: it''s counted as a vacant sale. A major renovation can reset the effective year built. Add the permits file, one row per permit, with the parcel ID. None? Skip it.

enrich.title: Enrichments
enrich.question: Add public data about each parcel?
enrich.lede: Distances to parks and water, building footprints, census figures and elevation, from public sources. Each is optional: turn on what helps your models. Bring in data downloads them as it runs; one that fails is skipped and said so, never stopping the run.

asSold.point1: A sale should be described as the property was **when it sold**: it may have changed since (an addition, a new roof, a regrade).
asSold.point2: Those characteristics are what the models **learn from**: they're what the price paid for.
asSold.point3: To value a parcel, the models use its characteristics **now**: the parcel files.
asSold.point4: So it's best practice to **freeze** a parcel's characteristics at the sale, and record them with the sale.
asSold.point5: Where a sale has no frozen characteristics, OAK box **assumes the parcel hasn't changed** and uses the parcel universe's. That's called *hydrating* the sales, filling them in from the parcels, and it's a modeling assumption.

1.name: Odd price per area, odd size
1.why: The size recorded is likely wrong: too small makes the price per area look high, too big makes it look low.
actions: Check the size and the characteristics as they were when it sold.
If the size is right, look for what else sets it apart: better materials, a better spot.

2.name: Low price, low per area
2.short: Not a market sale, or worse condition
2.why: Likely not a market sale: a foreclosure, a short sale, between family, a share of a property sold as the whole; or its condition is worse than recorded.
actions: Check the building''s age and condition.
Look at it in Street View beside its group: do the recorded characteristics match?
Check the deed for a foreclosure, a related party or a partial interest.

3.name: High price, high per area
3.why: Likely more than this parcel: several parcels on one deed, business assets or personal property in the price, a related party, or a partial interest''s price scaled to the whole.
actions: Check the deed for business assets or personal property, and the buyer and seller for a related party.
Check it wasn''t a sale of several parcels with this one''s size only (the related sales below).
For a partial interest: look for a control premium, which inflates a share''s price scaled to the whole.

4.name: Ordinary price, high per area
4.why: The finished area may be under-recorded, or there are upgrades not on record (a renovation, an addition).
actions: If they''re right, it may be ordinary variation: keep it.

5.name: Ordinary price, low per area
5.why: The finished area may be over-recorded, or the area includes another parcel''s (a sale of several parcels, the other way round).
actions: Check it wasn''t a sale of several parcels whose areas were added together (the related sales below).

other.name: No pattern fits (left in)
other.why: Far from its group by the ratio rules, but its price, price per area and size don''t fit any of the five patterns. It counts unless you exclude it.

standards.whoseLede: What the values are judged against. The IAAO''s fill in the next part, every figure changeable; or set your own (a state''s, or your office''s).

standards.title: The standards
standards.lede: Each standard is a set of targets, judged on the model groups you give it next. Change any figure, add or remove a standard.
standards.assignTitle: Which model groups each standard judges
standards.assignLede: Proposed from the groups'' names until you choose; a group is in one standard at most. A group in none is shown, not judged.
standards.source: The IAAO''s are from its Standard on Ratio Studies, exposure draft of May 2026 (sections 8.2 and 11, Appendices C and E).
standards.name: Name of the standard
standards.noneToAssign: No standards to give groups to: add one in the part before.
standards.prdNote: The PRD is reported, not judged: the draft no longer uses it for compliance. Hover a heading for what its target means.
standards.proposedNote: Once you choose a standard''s groups, every standard''s are as you see them here, no longer proposed.
standards.levelWhy: Values are, on the whole, near what parcels sell for. Missed only when the median''s whole 90% range is outside: a finding needs a high degree of confidence.
standards.codWhy: How far ratios stray from the median, on average, in percent. Above the range: not uniform enough. Below it: suspect, possibly sales chasing or a sample that isn''t representative.
standards.veiWhy: The primary vertical equity test: the highest-valued group''s median ratio less the lowest''s, percent of the median. Missed only when it''s significantly outside (the groups'' 90% ranges apart by more than the limit).
standards.prbWhy: How much ratios change when value doubles: negative, dearer parcels are valued relatively lower. Between the two ranges, neither met nor missed.
standards.minSalesWhy: Fewer sales: shown, not judged. (The VEI needs 20.)
standards.trim: Trim outlying ratios (beyond 1.5 × the interquartile range, at most a tenth of a group): the statistics without them are judged, every sale''s are shown beside them, and the trimmed sales are listed under Extreme ratios

run.lede: OpenAVMKit''s ratio and equity studies on the values, per model group and overall: a few seconds.
run.stale: Out of date: Check sales ran again, or a call changed since.

card.levelWhy: The median ratio (value ÷ sale price): are values near what parcels sell for? The standard asks for 0.90 to 1.10 (the whole confidence interval outside it fails).
card.uniformWhy: The COD: how far ratios typically sit from the median, as a % of it. Each group''s category sets its range (single-family 5 to 15, say); under the range is suspiciously even (sales chasing, or an unrepresentative sample).
card.horizontalWhy: Similar parcels valued alike? The CHD: within each group of similar parcels (Check sales'' equity clusters), every parcel, sold or not, the average distance of values from their median, percent: the middle group''s. The IAAO sets no target for it: shown, not judged.
card.verticalWhy: Are dearer parcels valued relatively higher or lower than cheaper ones? The VEI (the IAAO''s vertical equity test), or with too few sales for it, the PRB.
card.tooFew: Too few sales to judge: shown, not judged.
card.noSales: No sales in the window: not checked.

summary.ran: Checked {when} · {n, number} sales, {start} to {end}, {price} · the IAAO''s targets

table.note: ✓ / ✗ against the targets, on the sales left after trimming. "all" is every sale''s figure, beside it but never compared: the Standard says trimmed and untrimmed statistics can''t be read the same way. PRD and MKI are reported, not judged. Each header explains itself on hover.
table.mkiWhy: Modified Kakwani Index: the share of value against the share of price; 1 equitable, under 1 regressive. Reported, not judged.
table.medianWhy: Value over sale price: the middle one. 1.00 is values at what parcels sell for.
table.rangeWhy: The range the median is likely in, 90% confidence (the IAAO''s order statistics).
table.codWhy: Average distance of ratios from the median, percent of the median: above the category''s range, not uniform enough; below it, suspect.
table.prdWhy: Mean ratio over the price-weighted mean ratio: above 1, cheaper parcels valued relatively higher. Reported, not judged: the draft no longer uses it for compliance.
table.prbWhy: How much ratios change when value doubles: negative, dearer parcels valued relatively lower.
table.veiWhy: The primary vertical equity test: the highest-valued group''s median ratio less the lowest''s, percent of the median; needs 20 sales. Missed only when significantly outside ±10%.
table.trimmedWhy: Ratios far from the rest, left out: listed under Extreme ratios.

prices.title: Across prices: {name}
prices.lede: Each dot a sale: its ratio against its price. Black: the median ratio of each fifth of sales, by price. Green: the level the standard asks for.
prices.flat: Flat would be even: rising, dearer parcels are valued relatively higher; falling, lower.
prices.noVei: Too few sales for the VEI (it needs 20).

similar.title: Similar parcels, similar values?
similar.lede: Every parcel, sold or not: within each group of similar parcels (the equity clusters from Check sales), how far apart their values are. The IAAO sets no target for it: shown, not judged.
similar.wide: wide spread: groups too broad, or values uneven
similar.chdWhy: Within each group of similar parcels, the average distance of values from their median, percent: the middle group''s.

extreme.title: Extreme ratios
extreme.lede: Ratios far from the rest are left out of the statistics and listed here: each is a sale to question, or a value to fix.
extreme.none: No ratio was far enough from the rest to leave out.
extreme.nominal: a nominal price: not a sale
extreme.excluded: excluded: applies when Check sales runs again
extreme.note: Nominal price ({price}): not a market sale
extreme.untrimmed: Untrimmed, these would swing the statistics: a $10 deed makes a ratio in the tens of thousands.

map.lede: Each sale where its parcel is, coloured by its ratio. Clusters of red or blue show where values are off; scattered colour is noise or invalid sales.
map.label: Map of sales by ratio
map.none: The sales have no coordinates: the parcel universe needs shapes or latitude and longitude.
legend: 0.5 or less: value far under the price
2 or more: value far over the price

regions.lede: Comparing ratios across sale prices can''t tell an over-assessed house in a poor neighbourhood from a sale at a low price that wasn''t a market sale. Here sales are grouped by how dear their whole neighbourhood is (its median price level), not by their own price. If low-priced neighbourhoods have higher ratios too, the inequity is real; if this is flat while the VEI by sale isn''t, invalid sales are the likelier cause.
regions.choose: Choose a location field to group sales by neighbourhood.
regions.noLocations: There''s no location field yet: add one on Data › Location (a neighbourhood, a school district, a census block group), then check again.
regions.few: Too few to compare: {sales, number} sales in {regions, number} neighbourhoods (it needs 20 sales in 2 or more).
regions.reading: {sales, number} sales in {regions, number} neighbourhoods. From the cheapest neighbourhoods to the dearest, the median ratio moves {vei}: {verdict}.
regions.compare: By each sale''s own price, the VEI is {vei}.
regions.bySale: By its own price level (the VEI)

lag.lede: What''s around a parcel says a lot about its value. Each parcel can get the average of its nearest sales'' prices, and of its nearest parcels'' size, age and quality, as variables of their own: put them in a variable list like any other.
lag.how: OpenAVMKit''s spatial lag: the nearest of each, however far, the closer ones weighted more.
lag.nearestWhy: Averages the {k} nearest of each (OpenAVMKit''s default is 5).
lag.ownWhy: Only those picked are worked out and offered as variables.
lag.fieldsWhy: Numbers of the parcels around each one, besides those above.
lag.split: Worked out as the models are tried, after the sales are split: a sale''s nearby price comes only from sales outside its own fold, so a model never sees the price it''s judged on. A group with {k} or fewer sales to average has none (OpenAVMKit writes 0): let it borrow another group''s sales.

area.lede: Each parcel gets its area''s figures: the median sale price of its census tract, the median finished area of its neighbourhood (OpenAVMKit''s area statistics). Worked out as each run starts, after the sales are split: prices come from training sales only.
area.blankUnderUnit: sales or parcels in an area
area.underTip: Fewer than {min, number} sales: their price figures are blank (a model leans on a coarser area''s). The parcels in them, or in no area: {parcels, number}.
area.noLocations: No location fields to work them out by: add neighbourhoods on Data, or census tracts and block groups on Enrichments.

values.fillLede: Blanks the models can''t take: some models fail on a blank (the linear ones), others read it as unknown. Nothing in Check sales uses these: they only change what the models learn from.
values.runLede: Fills the blanks and folds the rare categories as set, on what Check sales wrote, then writes notebook 2''s output again (out/2-clean-sup.pickle): what the models start from.
values.stale: Out of date: Check sales ran again, or a fill or the folding changed.

vartest.runLede: Runs OpenAVMKit''s variable tests on each model group''s sales, every variable: then they''re shown one at a time, the evidence for the variable lists. A few seconds.
vartest.stale: Out of date: the fields were prepared again, the tests to run changed, or a variable was ticked that wasn''t tested.

pick.represented: Always: does it have values among the sales and the parcels?
pick.vif: How much of it do the other variables already explain?

vartest.howOverlaps: Moves most with (the VIF test judges overlap):
vartest.values: {passing, number} of {of, number} {of, plural, =1 {value passes} other {values pass}}
vartest.empty: Not tested in this model group: none of its sales has a value for {names}, so there''s nothing to test (and nothing for a model to learn from it here).
vartest.noneFail: Every variable passes this test in this model group.
vartest.failing: {n, number} {n, plural, =1 {variable fails} other {variables fail}} in this model group.

represented.lede: Does the variable have values (not zero, not blank) among the sales and among the parcels? One missing from either can''t be learned from, or can''t be applied.
represented.rule: Passes with any value in both the sales and the parcels.

corr.lede: Does the variable move with price? Its correlation with sale price, either way: whether it overlaps other variables isn''t judged here, the VIF test does that. Press how › on a row to see what it moves with most.
corr.rule: Passes with a correlation with price of {t} or more, either way.

vif.lede: Variance inflation: how much of it the other variables already explain (1: none; 5 to 10: high; over 10: very high). Redundant variables make a model unstable and hard to read. The worst is dropped, again and again; yes/no variables aren''t tested.
vif.rule: Passes if it survives the drops (VIF under {t}).

vartest.verdictLede: OpenAVMKit scores each variable on the tests (each weighted), then keeps the set that predicts best in cross-validation: its pick per model group.

lists.lede: Each model takes its variables from a list. A list has a name, a type (regression or machine learning) and the model groups it''s for; one list can serve several. Beside each variable, its test scores and what''s recommended for the list''s type.
lists.name: Name

rule.regression: Recommended for a regression: in the sales, moves with price (0.10 or more either way), overlaps nothing much (VIF 10 or under), no blanks, and not a category with many values.
rule.ml: Recommended for machine learning: anything that''s in the sales. ML models find their own way with weak or overlapping variables; a category with many values is the one thing to spare: CatBoost slows with each.

lists.written: Written to OpenAVMKit''s settings as variable_lists, each model pointing at its list. A list''s ticks are the same for every model group it''s for: for a group''s own variables, make it a list of its own.
lists.notTested: The variables haven''t been tested yet: the recommendations go by blanks and categories alone until they are (Test the variables).

warn.few_sales: {group} has {sales, number} sales for this list''s {vars, number} variables: a regression wants about 10 sales a variable. A shorter list of its own would suit it better.
warn.blanks: Has blanks, so a regression leaves it out: {names}. Fill them (Fill blanks) to use them.
warn.many_values: {ml, select, true {Categories with many values (CatBoost slows with each): {names}.} other {Categories with many values (each value a column of its own, few sales behind each): {names}.}}

lists.none: No variable lists yet. Each model takes its variables from one: add a list, choose its type and the model groups it''s for, then tick its variables (Tick the recommended starts you off).
lists.chooseGroups: Choose the model groups it''s for: their models can take it.
lists.missing: Not loaded: {fields}. The models do better with them (Data › Building).
lists.noVariables: No variables found yet: prepare the fields first.

stack.title: Locations, broadest first
stack.how: {engine, select, local_area {Local area values each parcel by its area''s median price per area, at the finest level with enough sales; an area with too few falls back to the level above it.} other {Multi-MRA fits a regression in each area of the finest level with 15 or more sales; an area with fewer falls back to the level above it, and the whole model group last.}}
stack.splits: {n, number} {n, plural, =1 {area spans} other {areas span}} more than one {above}
stack.noneLeft: Every location field is in the stack.
stack.noFields: No location fields: add a neighborhood or district on Data › Locations, a map layer, or census areas (Data › Enrichments).
stack.written: Written finest first, as OpenAVMKit reads it: {fields}.

small.lede: Too few sales to learn from or to judge them by, or values that make no sense (a holdout median ratio outside 0.5 to 2, or a value below zero). Left unvalued unless you choose to model them anyway: their parcels get no model value, and the report says so.

flags.too_few: {n, number} {n, plural, =1 {sale} other {sales}}: too few to model
flags.no_values: no model produced values for it
flags.no_holdout: no sales held out to judge it by

small.cantModel: No model produced values for it: it can only be left unvalued.
small.unvalued: Left unvalued: {parcels, number} {parcels, plural, =1 {parcel} other {parcels}} in {n, number} {n, plural, =1 {group} other {groups}} ({groups}). Their model value is blank; the report and the export list them.
small.blanked: {n, number} {n, plural, =1 {parcel} other {parcels}} in groups modeled anyway came out below zero: left blank, and counted.
small.neverBelow: A value below zero never ships: the parcel stays blank and is counted.
small.applies: Applies when the values are made (Finalize): the try models every group, to judge it.
small.title: Groups the models can't be trusted on.

final.lede: Trains each group''s models once more, on all of its sales, and values every parcel: the values that ship. The groups Small groups leaves unvalued are skipped; a value below zero is left blank.
final.stale: Something changed since the values were made (the try, a small group''s choice, or Evaluate''s window or standards): finalize again.
final.valuesLede: The model values against what parcels sold for, judged as Evaluate judges the roll''s, with the roll''s on the same sales beside them.

setWhy.oof: Each sale valued by a model that never saw it: the cross-validation''s models, each trained without the sales it values. Every sale, honestly judged.
setWhy.held: The sales the final models never trained on (after the valuation date), valued by the final models.
setWhy.valued: Every sale, valued by the final models, which trained on most of them: the values as they ship, but flattering.

final.noRoll: No existing values loaded to compare with (Data › Assessed values).
final.changeWhy: The median of each parcel''s model value over its roll value, less one.
final.totals: {valued, number} of {parcels, number} parcels got a model value.

why.ratio: Each sale in the set judged on, coloured by its ratio: model value ÷ price. Clusters of red or blue show where the values are off.
why.value: Every parcel, coloured by its model value per finished area, in tenths of the parcels shown: cheap to dear.
why.change: Every parcel, coloured by its model value against the roll''s: blue lower, red higher.

model.modelsLede: Each modeled group has its own models, one group at a time: the button at the bottom right goes on to the next. Every group starts with LightGBM, MRA and Multi-MRA; add, remove or rename them. Each takes its variables from a variable list; Multi-MRA and Local area read a stack of locations too. The ensemble is the median of a group''s models, leaving out any that don''t help; the roll is audited beside them on the study set, never in it.
model.configLater: Its defaults; change them once it''s added.

config.title: {name}: its own settings
config.logWhy: Its values can''t come out below zero, and an extra square foot adds a percentage rather than a fixed amount.
config.interceptWhy: A base value every parcel gets. Without it, a parcel with every variable at zero is worth zero.
config.interactionsWhy: Categories × size multiplies each land category by land area, and each building category by finished area: a category then changes the price per square foot, not a flat amount.
config.optimizeVarsWhy: In each area with enough sales, drops the variables that don''t help that area''s regression. Slower.
config.trialsWhy: How many settings it tries while tuning itself: fewer is faster, more can fit better.
config.gpu: Use the graphics card if there is one
config.gpuWhy: Faster where there''s a suitable one; the processor otherwise.
config.warnLog: Without log price it can value parcels below zero.
config.warnIntercept: Only if a parcel with nothing (no land, no building) is worth nothing.
config.warnTrials: Few trials: quick, but it may not tune well.

model.noModels: No models: add one, or untick the group on Model groups › Check them.

warn.kind_mismatch: {kind, select, ml {{engine} is a regression; this is a machine-learning list: overlapping variables and many categories make its coefficients unreliable.} other {{engine} is a machine-learning model on a regression list: it''ll run, but it could use more variables than this.}}
warn.list_missing: Its list was removed: it takes the group''s first list of its type.
warn.list_empty: Its variable list has no variables: tick some on Variables › Variable lists.
warn.no_list: No variable list: make one on Variables › Variable lists.
warn.blanks_left_out: Leaves out {n, number} {n, plural, =1 {variable} other {variables}} of its list with blanks: a regression can''t take a blank.
warn.no_locations: {engine, select, local_area {Local area needs at least one location level.} other {No location levels: it fits one regression for the whole group, as MRA does.}}

model.tooFew: too few to model: no model values
model.salesCount: {n, number} {n, plural, =1 {sale} other {sales}} to learn from
model.tryLede: Trains each model on each model group and checks it on sales it never saw (5-fold cross-validation). Nothing is written to the roll: this is a try.
model.stale: Out of date: the fields were prepared again, or a variable or model changed.
model.howLede: OpenAVMKit''s benchmark for each model group: the IAAO figures on each set of sales, or the academic ones, each untrimmed then trimmed. Click a heading to sort; drag a column''s edge to widen it. The ensemble is what would ship.

setWhy.holdout: Each sale valued by a model that never saw it (5-fold cross-validation). The roll isn''t here: this holdout is OpenAVMKit''s own draw, and the roll''s values may have been made with these very sales.
setWhy.post_val: Sales after the valuation date: no model saw them.
setWhy.study: Sales in the year before the valuation date: the IAAO frame for auditing a roll. The roll is here, beside the models; each model is judged by its holdout predictions, on sales it never saw, so like for like.

empty.post_val: No sales after the valuation date.
empty.study: No sales in the year before the valuation date, so the roll can''t be audited beside the models. Move the valuation date, or bring in later sales.

how.academicWhy: How far each prediction is from its price, as a statistician would judge it: in percent and in dollars.

tip.utility: OpenAVMKit''s score for choosing between models (utility_score): lower is better.
tip.sales: The sales the figures are on.
tip.salesTrimmed: The sales left once the outlying ratios (beyond 1.5 × the interquartile range) are left out.
tip.parcels: Parcels in the model group the model values.
tip.median: Value ÷ price, the middle one: the level. IAAO''s range: 0.90 to 1.10.
tip.cod: Coefficient of dispersion: how far ratios stray from the median, in percent. Its range depends on the model group''s property category (Evaluate).
tip.prd: Price-related differential: the mean ratio over the value-weighted mean. Reported, not judged.
tip.prb: Price-related bias: how ratios change as value doubles. Good within ±0.05; unacceptable beyond ±0.10.
tip.vei: Vertical equity index: how ratios drift from the cheapest sales to the dearest, in percent. Near 0 is even.
tip.veiSig: How sure the VEI''s drift is real (vei_sig).
tip.chd: Coefficient of horizontal dispersion: how the values of alike parcels spread. Figured on all the parcels, so only on the study set.
tip.mape: Mean absolute percentage error: how far, on average, a value is from its price.
tip.mse: Mean squared error, in dollars squared.
tip.rmse: Root mean squared error: a typical miss, in dollars.
tip.slope: Value against price, through the origin: 1 is no tilt.

model.nextSlice: Finalizing (the values written, and checked as step 4 checks the roll''s) comes next.

outliers.noneCommon: Nothing the sales share lines up with the models' error beyond chance.

outliers.notClustered: On the map, the errors aren't more alike between neighbours than chance would make them.

fields.title: Welcome to OAK box
fields.lede:
OAK box helps you build models. It needs two datasets for that: a **sales record** and a **parcel universe**

The **sales record** is what every parcel sold for and when (and ideally, what each parcel was like when it sold)

The **parcel universe** is every parcel, sold and unsold, as it is now.
Both are needed to build a model. We''ll start with the parcel universe.

details.title: More details
details.lede: Where each parcel is, what kind of property it is, any other columns you want, the values it has now, and map layers. A short part each; one you don''t have can be left.

condos.title: Condo units
condos.lede: Condos, and anything else on the roll that isn''t on the map: units with a parcel ID of their own but no shape, because they share a parcel. Here OAK box learns how to find each unit''s parcel, so the unit is placed, measured and valued like any other parcel.

bring.title: Inputs
bring.lede: OpenAVMKit reads the files as Data describes them and joins them into one table of every parcel (the parcel universe) and one of every sale. It also works out what it can on its own: coordinates, building ages, land areas, and the public data you asked for.

groups.title: Model groups
groups.lede: Not every parcel sells the same way: a condo isn''t valued like a farm. Model groups split the parcels into kinds that sell alike, so each kind gets its own models, and its own ratio study.

sales.title: Sales
sales.lede: Only fair, open-market sales are evidence of what parcels are worth. This step decides which sales count, and brings their prices to the valuation date.

check.title: Evaluate
check.lede: Before modeling anything, how good are the values you have now? This step checks the existing roll, and any other values you loaded, against what parcels actually sold for: the IAAO ratio study.

variables.title: Variables
variables.lede: Models learn from the parcels'' characteristics: size, age, quality, location. This step gets those fields ready, finds which ones carry information about price, and puts them into the lists the models use.

values.title: Models
values.lede: This is where the values are made. Each model group gets its models; they''re tried, judged as Evaluate judges the roll, and the best are combined into one value for every parcel.

report.title: Report
report.lede: The values out of OAK box: as a file for your CAMA system or GIS, and as a report that says plainly how good they are.

more_files.title: More files
more_files.lede: Files with more about each parcel or each sale (building details, deeds…), or more of them (older sales, a second parcel file). First add them all; then each gets a part of its own, to say what it''s about, how it joins, and to check its rows find theirs.

big_five.title: Big five
big_five.lede: The five things a model leans on most: how big the building is, how big its land is, how old it is, how well it''s built and what condition it''s in. Building size is required; land size is worked out from the shapes if you leave it out; the other three are strongly recommended. One short part each.

nav.projectsFoot: Each opens where you last were in it. Nothing in this one stops or is lost.
